result.explanation: Each event is serialized independently. Scalars use their JSON representations, strings receive ECMAScript-compatible escaping, arrays preserve order, and objects are recursively serialized after lexical key sorting. The opaque state remains null.
result.program: function solve({config,state,event}){function enc(v){if(v===null)return"null";var t=typeof v;if(t==="string")return'"'+v.replace(/[\\"\u0000-\u001f]/g,function(c){if(c==='\\')return'\\\\';if(c==='"')return'\\"';if(c==='\b')return'\\b';if(c==='\f')return'\\f';if(c==='\n')return'\\n';if(c==='\r')return'\\r';if(c==='\t')return'\\t';return'\\u'+c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(4,'0')})+'"';if(t==='number'||t==='boolean')return String(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=[];for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a.push(enc(v[i]));return'['+a.join(',')+']'}var k=Object.keys(v).sort(),a=[];for(var j=0;j<k.length;j++)a.push(enc(k[j])+':'+enc(v[k[j]]));return'{'+a.join(',')+'}'}return{state:null,output:{key:enc(event.value)}}}
